metadata.title: Gierer & Meinhardt (1972) Kybernetik 12:30-39 Hydra vulgaris Short-Range Activator / Long-Range Inhibitor Morphogenesis Reference Dataset

sources.citation: Gierer A, Meinhardt H (1972). A theory of biological pattern formation. Kybernetik 12(1):30-39.
Meinhardt H, Gierer A (1974). Applications of a theory of biological pattern formation based on lateral inhibition. Journal of Cell Science 15(2):321-346.

Meinhardt H (1993). A model for pattern formation of hypostome, tentacles, and foot in hydra: how to form structures close to each other, how to form them at a distance. Developmental Biology 157(2):321-333.
Meinhardt H (2012). Modeling pattern formation in hydra: a route to understanding essential steps in development. International Journal of Developmental Biology 56(6-8):447-462.

hydra_vulgaris_specimen.species: Hydra vulgaris (Freshwater cnidarian polyp, dark-field whole-mount showing basal foot, body column, apical hypostome, and 6 radial tentacles)

governing_equations.activator_pde: da/dt = rho_0 * rho(x) + c * rho(x) * a^2 / h - mu_a * a + D_a * d^2a/dx^2
governing_equations.inhibitor_pde: dh/dt = c_prime * rho(x) * a^2 - mu_h * h + D_h * d^2h/dx^2
governing_equations.boundary_conditions: Zero-flux Neumann boundary conditions: da/dx = 0, dh/dx = 0 at x = 0 (apical head) and x = L (basal foot)

linear_stability_invariants.homogeneous_stability_condition: mu_h > mu_a (inhibitor turns over faster than activator so tr(J_0) = mu_a - mu_h < 0 and det(J_0) = mu_a * mu_h > 0)
linear_stability_invariants.lateral_inhibition_range_condition: l_a = sqrt(D_a / mu_a) << l_h = sqrt(D_h / mu_h) (short-range autocatalytic activation coupled with long-range lateral inhibition)

hydra_regimes_and_experiments._parity_note: Pass 3 (2026-10-19): values below are the ones actually used by 1972-gierer-hydra-activator-inhibitor.py and are asserted in --self-test check 9 (Pass 1/2 placeholders N=60, slope -0.15, ring 50, recovery 0.90 and domain lengths {20..95} did not match the code).

intact_polar_column.description: Gierer & Meinhardt (1972) Fig. 2: Shallow source-density gradient rho(x) = 1.0 * (1 - 0.20 * x/(N-1)) on a 40-cell column (D_a = 0.03, D_h = 6.0) triggers a single tall apical hypostome activator peak at x = 0.

bisection_regeneration.description: Gierer & Meinhardt (1972) Fig. 3: Surgical removal of the apical head half (cutting at x = 20 = 0.5*L); removal of long-range inhibitor allows the new apical cut end of the basal fragment (20 cells) to regenerate a hypostome activator peak.

tentacle_ring_periodic.description: Meinhardt (1993) Dev. Biol. 157:321-333: Periodic activator-inhibitor instability around the circular sub-hypostomal ring (circumference C = 64 cells, periodic boundary conditions, D_a = 0.015, D_h = 0.45) forms 6 quasi-evenly spaced tentacle primordia matching the adult Hydra vulgaris specimen.

allometric_domain_scaling.description: Peak insertion with ring circumference L in {22, 33, 44, 54, 64, 76, 88} cells under uniform source density rho(x) = 1.0: number of activator peaks scales approximately linearly with L / lambda (observed counts from the seeded runs).

equal_diffusion_negative_control.description: Equal-diffusion ablation control (D_a = D_h = 0.015, d = 1.0 < d_c = 5.8284): random perturbations decay exponentially to the spatially uniform equilibrium with zero pattern peaks.

three_system_cylindrical_shell.description: Pass 3 (2026-10-19): reduced Meinhardt (1993, 2012) coupled head / tentacle / foot activator-inhibitor loops with a slowly adapting source density, integrated on a finite-difference surface of revolution whose radius profile r(s) is measured on hydra_vulgaris_specimen.jpg (Euclidean distance transform along the PCA body axis). Functional forms of the couplings (Hill gating H_t(sigma) = sigma^p/(sigma_t^p + sigma^p), head suppression 1/(1 + kappa_a a), foot drive 1/(1 + (sigma/sigma_f)^p_f)) are this implementation's reduced choices, not digitised from the papers.
three_system_cylindrical_shell.geometry: Laplace-Beltrami operator (1/r) d/ds(r du/ds) + (1/r^2) d2u/dtheta2 on an N_s x N_theta grid; exact Fourier step in theta, backward-Euler tridiagonal step in s, explicit reactions (dt = 0.5).
three_system_cylindrical_shell.scale_calibration: L = 90 cells chosen so that the shell's intrinsic tentacle spacing (~8.1 cells, set by l_c = sqrt(D_c/mu_h) = 3.87 cells) equals the specimen's inter-tentacle spacing / body length (0.092). The tentacle COUNT is therefore a geometric consequence of this calibration (7 vs specimen 6); the ring axial position, uniform cap, foot position and regeneration order are uncalibrated predictions.
three_system_cylindrical_shell.tentacle_firing_threshold_formula: w_c = (mu_a / 2) * sqrt(rho_c / (c * mu_h * rho_b)); the homogeneous off state of a thresholded subsystem exists iff its drive w <= w_c (Lean: meinhardt_three_system_off_state_discriminant_antitone)

specimen_references.ring_attachment_offset_frac: hypostome tip -> tentacle attachment distance / full body length, measured on the specimen by measure_specimen_body_profile (approx. 0.070)
specimen_references.caveat: All measured on a 2D projection of a tilted, contracted polyp; used as reference bands, not exact targets.

expected_outcomes.hypostome: single azimuthally uniform cap at s = 0 (CV_theta < 0.05)
expected_outcomes.tentacle_ring: one sub-hypostomal row of 5-8 primordia inside the specimen attachment band and inside the analytic firing band phi_t > w_c
expected_outcomes.foot: uniform basal disc at s = L
expected_outcomes.ablation_kappa_a_0: tentacle activator leaks into the hypostome (>5x apex level) and the ring shifts apically
expected_outcomes.regeneration: basal half regenerates a hypostome at the cut (t_head < t_ring) and a new tentacle ring directly below it
